plain_language_rule: No qualifying BNR-Heart evidence was detected on the certificate.
why_this_class: The automated rules found no explicit AMI, qualifying ischaemic/coronary Heart wording, or qualifying sudden-cardiac-death evidence.

plain_language_rule: Heart-related context was detected, but it does not by itself support BNR-Heart as the approximate underlying cause.
why_this_class: This is the general context/mention layer. Stronger rules can overwrite it when the certificate position and wording justify greater confidence.

plain_language_rule: Current direct BNR-Heart wording appears only in Part II.
why_this_class: Part II records contributing conditions outside the stated Part I causal sequence, so a Part-II-only Heart statement is retained as a mention rather than treated as approximate underlying cause.

plain_language_rule: Only historical BNR-Heart evidence is present outside a current Part I Heart sequence.
why_this_class: A previous, prior, remote or old Heart condition does not establish a current BNR-Heart underlying cause.

plain_language_rule: Sudden cardiac death is written above another Part I cause on a certificate whose line order is preserved.
why_this_class: The certificate itself places another condition lower in the stated causal chain. Sudden cardiac death alone is therefore not promoted to approximate Heart underlying cause.

plain_language_rule: Current direct BNR-Heart evidence appears somewhere in Part I, but a simple rule does not resolve it as the approximate underlying cause.
why_this_class: The Heart diagnosis is real certificate evidence, but another lower Part I condition or structural issue leaves meaningful uncertainty.

plain_language_rule: The certificate explicitly gives Heart and Stroke as alternatives, for example 'heart attack or stroke'.
why_this_class: The combined circulatory endpoint may be supported, but the Heart subtype cannot be resolved confidently from alternative wording.

plain_language_rule: Current BNR-Heart and BNR-Stroke evidence both appear in Part I.
why_this_class: Both surveillance families are present in the stated causal sequence, so Heart is retained as possible rather than forced to be the sole subtype.

plain_language_rule: Sudden cardiac death appears alone or as the lowest Part I condition, or the original certificate line order is not preserved.
why_this_class: Sudden cardiac death is within the historical BNR fatal-event ascertainment scope but is less specific than explicit AMI/IHD evidence.

plain_language_rule: Historical-only Heart evidence appears in Part I with no separate current Heart evidence.
why_this_class: A historical Heart condition in the stated causal sequence is stronger than a Part-II history, but it still does not establish a current acute Heart underlying cause.

plain_language_rule: Current direct BNR-Heart evidence is on the lowest used Part I line of a reasonably formed multi-line certificate.
why_this_class: The lowest used Part I line is the usual starting point for underlying-cause selection when the reported sequence is acceptable. The BNR approximation stops at Likely because it does not perform full formal ICD sequence validation.

plain_language_rule: Explicit AMI appears above a lowest Part I ischaemic/coronary Heart condition.
why_this_class: WHO mortality linkage rules support resolving the IHD/AMI combination toward acute myocardial infarction.

plain_language_rule: Current BNR-Heart evidence appears above hypertension on the lowest used Part I line.
why_this_class: WHO mortality linkage rules support assigning the ischaemic Heart disease rather than hypertension in this combination.

plain_language_rule: Current BNR-Heart evidence appears above atherosclerosis on the lowest used Part I line.
why_this_class: WHO mortality linkage rules support assigning the ischaemic Heart disease rather than atherosclerosis in this combination.

plain_language_rule: A record that would otherwise be Clear is capped at Likely because the original certificate line structure is concatenated or uncertain.
why_this_class: Strong disease wording remains useful, but lost or uncertain line order prevents the highest confidence level.

plain_language_rule: One clean Part I line contains current direct BNR-Heart evidence, with no competing Heart/Stroke ambiguity.
why_this_class: With a single preserved Part I cause and no obvious structural ambiguity, the certificate provides the strongest evidence available to this BNR approximation.
